hook: Reading about yawning makes people yawn. A scientist measured it.
twist: Everyone says we yawn for oxygen. Robert Provine tested it in 1987: breathing pure oxygen or extra carbon dioxide didn't change yawning. Then he measured contagion: 55% yawned at a yawn video (21% at smiles), and 30% yawned just reading about yawning (11% reading about hiccups). The viewer is the experiment.
angle: The Brain insists it yawns for oxygen; the experiments say no, and then make the viewer yawn. Big numbers: 55% vs 21%, 30% vs 11%.
why_now: Scout 2026-10-06 (YouTube Data API, Shorts since mid-2024, query 'why do we yawn'): top 32.5M ('The Yawn That Locked Her Jaw', Zack D. Evergreen, proven demand; the interactive angle is the outlier format.
